summary: This bill amends federal law to require the National Survey on Drug Use and Health to include Puerto Rico starting in fiscal year 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the inclusion of Puerto Rico in the annual National Survey on Drug Use and Health starting in fiscal year 2026. This federal survey is conducted by the government, and adding a new territory will likely require additional resources, funding, or personnel for data collection in Puerto Rico. While the existing survey already operates nationwide, extending it explicitly to Puerto Rico represents a minor expansion of government spending on public health data collection activities. The impact is tangential and small-scale, not a major budgetary shift.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, tax policies, or any fiscal mechanisms related to revenue collection. It solely addresses data collection requirements under existing public health law.
